title: OpenAI releases ChatGPT as a public research preview
description: OpenAI released ChatGPT to the public as a free research preview built on a model in the GPT-3.5 series. This row is the registry origin point, marking the first date on which a general audience could obtain conversational answers to information queries outside a search engine. The vendor post confirms the release, and the date recorded here comes from contemporaneous reporting rather than a dateline on the vendor page, so the row is tagged vendor_announced.

title: Google announces Search Generative Experience at I/O 2023
description: At Google I/O 2023, Google announced the Search Generative Experience, an AI generated summary panel placed above the classic result list. Access was gated behind a Search Labs waitlist at announcement, so availability spread over a period Google did not bound publicly. SGE is the direct ancestor of AI Overviews and is recorded here so the AI Overviews rows have a starting point.

title: OpenAI releases GPT-4o as the ChatGPT default model
description: OpenAI announced GPT-4o, a multimodal flagship model that became the default in ChatGPT for free and paid users. Availability was staged across text, vision, voice, and API access over the weeks following the announcement, so the rollout window is wider than the single announcement date. The date recorded here comes from contemporaneous reporting rather than a dateline on the vendor page.

title: Google launches AI Overviews for all United States searchers
description: At Google I/O 2024, Google announced that AI Overviews would launch to all users in the United States, retiring the Search Generative Experience label. Google stated the feature would reach hundreds of millions of US searchers during the following week, so the announcement date and the date any individual query began returning an AI Overview differ. This row records the announcement date and does not assert a completion date.

title: Google expands AI Overviews to more than 100 additional countries
description: Google expanded AI Overviews to more than 100 additional countries and territories and to several new languages, stating the surface then reached more than one billion monthly users. The expansion was described as rolling out from this date rather than completing on it, and per country availability was not enumerated by the vendor. Any panel that treats a market as AI Overviews enabled from this date is making an assumption the source does not support.

title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT search with real time web retrieval
description: OpenAI launched ChatGPT search, adding real time web retrieval with inline source links to ChatGPT. At launch the feature was limited to Plus and Team subscribers, and it was extended to all logged in users in February 2025. This row records the initial launch; the later extension is not separately seeded.

title: Google introduces AI Mode as a Search Labs experiment
description: Google introduced AI Mode, a conversational search surface reached from a dedicated tab, as a Search Labs experiment for Google One AI Premium subscribers in the United States. The same announcement moved AI Overviews to Gemini 2.0 for harder query classes. The vendor page carries the announcement date and Labs availability began the same day.

title: Google March 2025 core update
description: Google released the March 2025 core update, announced on the Search Status Dashboard as applying globally to all languages and regions. Google estimated a rollout of up to two weeks, and the dashboard recorded completion on 27 March 2025 at 05:35 US/Pacific. Both the start and completion timestamps are vendor published.

title: Google releases Gemini 2.5 Pro Experimental
description: Google released Gemini 2.5 Pro Experimental, the first model in the Gemini 2.5 family, described by the vendor as a thinking model that reasons before responding. The model reached the Gemini consumer app for Advanced subscribers at announcement and later became the model behind AI Mode in Search. The vendor page carries the announcement date.

title: Google makes AI Mode available to all United States Search users
description: At Google I/O 2025, Google announced that AI Mode would be available to all Search users in the United States, moving it out of Search Labs, with a custom version of Gemini 2.5 behind it. Google stated the tab would appear for US searches during that week, so per user availability lagged the announcement by an unstated interval. This row records the announcement date.

title: Google June 2025 core update
description: Google released the June 2025 core update, announced on the Search Status Dashboard as applying globally to all languages and regions. Google estimated a rollout of up to three weeks, and the dashboard recorded completion on 17 July 2025 at 01:00 US/Pacific. Both the start and completion timestamps are vendor published.

title: Perplexity launches Comet browser to Max subscribers and waitlist
description: Perplexity launched Comet, a browser with an assistant embedded in every new tab, initially to Perplexity Max subscribers and selected waitlist participants. Distribution was invitation gated at launch, so the population able to reach the surface grew on a schedule Perplexity did not publish. The date recorded here comes from contemporaneous reporting rather than a dateline on the vendor page.

title: OpenAI releases GPT-5 and makes it the ChatGPT default
description: OpenAI released GPT-5 and made it the default in ChatGPT, replacing the previous model picker with automatic routing across fast and reasoning variants. The change altered which model answers a given ChatGPT prompt without any user action, which matters for any measurement series that assumes a fixed model behind the surface. The date recorded here comes from contemporaneous reporting rather than a dateline on the vendor page.

title: Google August 2025 spam update
description: Google released the August 2025 spam update, announced on the Search Status Dashboard as applying globally and to all languages. The dashboard recorded completion on 22 September 2025 at 00:00 US/Pacific, giving a rollout of roughly four weeks. Google published no separate guidance alongside this update.

title: Perplexity makes Comet free worldwide
description: Perplexity removed the subscription and waitlist gate on Comet and made the browser free worldwide. This changes the addressable population of the surface rather than its answer behavior, and it is recorded separately from the limited launch for that reason. The date recorded here comes from contemporaneous reporting rather than a dateline on the vendor page.

title: Google releases Gemini 3 and deploys it into Search
description: Google released Gemini 3 and deployed it into Google Search, the Gemini app, and developer surfaces on the same day. A frontier model release that lands in Search on its announcement date is the case this registry exists to capture, because a model event and a search side answer change share one timestamp and cannot be separated by date alone. The vendor page carries the announcement date.

title: Google December 2025 core update
description: Google released the December 2025 core update, announced on the Search Status Dashboard as applying globally to all languages and regions. Google estimated a rollout of up to three weeks, and the dashboard recorded completion on 29 December 2025 at 11:00 US/Pacific. This rollout shares a start date with the GPT-5.2 release, which any event study over this window should treat as a confound rather than a coincidence to ignore.

title: OpenAI releases GPT-5.2
description: OpenAI released GPT-5.2 and began rolling it out in ChatGPT starting with paid plans, with immediate availability in the API. The release shares a start date with the December 2025 Google core update, so volatility observed in this window cannot be assigned to either event without separating the surfaces first. The date recorded here comes from contemporaneous reporting rather than a dateline on the vendor page.

title: OpenAI releases GPT-5.4 with native computer use
description: OpenAI released GPT-5.4 in ChatGPT, the API, and Codex, adding native computer use and a context window of up to one million tokens. GPT-5.4 mini followed on 17 March 2026 and reached free tier ChatGPT users, so the model behind free tier answers changed on a later date than the flagship release. The date recorded here comes from contemporaneous reporting rather than a dateline on the vendor page.

title: Google March 2026 spam update
description: Google released the March 2026 spam update, announced on the Search Status Dashboard as applying globally and to all languages. The dashboard recorded completion on 25 March 2026 at 07:30 US/Pacific, a rollout of under one day. It began three days before the March 2026 core update, so the two rollouts overlap and should not be read as a single event.

title: Google March 2026 core update
description: Google released the March 2026 core update, announced on the Search Status Dashboard as applying globally to all languages and regions. Google estimated a rollout of up to two weeks, and the dashboard recorded completion on 8 April 2026 at 06:00 US/Pacific. The March 2026 spam update had completed only two days before this rollout began.

title: Google makes AI Mode the global Search default at I/O 2026
description: At Google I/O 2026, Google announced that AI Mode becomes the default Search experience globally, with Gemini 3.5 Flash behind it, alongside a rebuilt search box and persistent information agents. Google stated the agents would reach Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in the United States over the following months, so the announcement date and the date any given user saw the new default differ. This row records the announcement date and does not assert a completion date.

title: Google May 2026 core update
description: Google released the May 2026 core update, announced on the Search Status Dashboard as applying globally to all languages and regions. Google estimated a rollout of up to two weeks, and the dashboard recorded completion on 2 June 2026 at 05:40 US/Pacific. The rollout began two days after the I/O 2026 announcement that AI Mode becomes the global Search default, so ranking movement and surface composition changed in the same window.

title: Google June 2026 spam update
description: Google released the June 2026 spam update, announced on the Search Status Dashboard as applying globally and to all languages. The dashboard recorded completion on 26 June 2026 at 10:00 US/Pacific. This is the most recent confirmed Google ranking update in the registry as of the seed date.

title: OpenAI opens general availability of GPT-5.6
description: OpenAI opened general availability of GPT-5.6 across its Sol, Terra, and Luna variants. A limited preview had been released on 26 June 2026 to a small group of partner organizations behind a United States government safety review, so the model was serving production traffic for roughly two weeks before general access. The date recorded here comes from contemporaneous reporting rather than a dateline on the vendor page.
